heterogeneity_trace.conclusion: heterogeneity that EXISTS (v0, connectivity W, spike timing) is INSUFFICIENT to differentiate the integrated E count in RFoff; count degeneracy is produced by (class-identical Izhikevich params) x (uniform per-unit drive). In RFon the same degeneracy holds everywhere except the graded-drive V1 target units.

claim_3_omission_drive_vs_rate_decrement.claim: identical E counts (var=0) + 185x energy difference => omission phenotype dominated by drive construction

A_omission_drive_diff.nature: spatially uniform global withdrawal (p2 slot zeroed for every unit) - a global flash-off, not a local retinotopic omission

B_omission_drive_diff.nature: retinotopically localized to 3 V1 L4 target units

coupling.note: the ~185x drive difference maps to ~100x omission-effect difference; omission amplitude is a near-linear readout of removed drive energy

claim_3_omission_drive_vs_rate_decrement.mechanism: RFoff omission = uniform global drive step-down; every E unit loses identical drive (26550) and shows identical decrement (7 spikes; -1.51 Hz). The -2.6..-3.2 Hz area decrements and the zero-variance E counts are both direct consequences of the drive construction (uniform x all 400 units x amplitude 5.0). Hierarchy modulates the decrement's area distribution (V1 -2.64 vs PFC -3.19) but the dominant control variable is the drive.

verdict.definition: the omission phenotype amplitude, its spatial uniformity, and the zero E spike-count variance are controlled by how external drive is constructed (uniform global vs retinotopic graded) and by its energy, not by cortical-hierarchy/HDP mechanism
supporting_facts: 185.55x (184.55x exact) drive-energy gap between RFoff (42.48M) and RFon (230.18k) in the AAAB trial
RFoff omission removes identical 26550 drive from all 400 units (global flash-off); RFon removes 15.5-26.6k from only 3 V1 target units (local)
omission effect scales ~linearly with removed drive energy: RFoff -2.6..-3.2 Hz vs RFon -0.004..-0.027 Hz (~1%)

E spike counts have exact zero variance in RFoff because count is a degenerate observable of (class-identical a/b/c/d + uniform drive); the 0.31% raster-timing jitter from v0/connectivity does not change counts
HDP H is constant in A (1.02897) over the recorded window - no adaptation dynamics driving the phenotype in the retained samples
caveats: hierarchy is NOT inert: area decrements differ (V1 -2.64 vs PFC -3.19 Hz) within RFoff, so connectivity modulates the response
per-unit synaptic input and population V_m are UNRESOLVED (no full-population current/membrane traces retained)
per-unit H heterogeneity UNRESOLVED (H recorded as population scalar)
B omission effect (~0.01-0.03 Hz) is near the noise floor; B's omission phenotype is essentially ABSENT, consistent with drive-energy starvation rather than an RF-specific mechanism

recommendation.v0.1: record as F-01 in the failure atlas (MODEL property: drive-construction dominates the omission phenotype; RF factor confounded with 185x drive-energy difference)
recommendation.v0.2_requirement: BEFORE interpreting RF effects, Factorial v0.2 design MUST include a drive-energy-matched control (e.g., RFoff at matched total energy, or normalized per-unit drive, or energy-normalized RFon) so the RF factor is not co-varied with drive magnitude; this is a design constraint, not a model repair - do not alter the v0.1 model

limitations_summary: external_drive_examples.npz retained only AAAB/AXAB; per-slot energy derived from slot-index windows at dt=0.1ms
A retains spike counts only (no rasters); raster-timing analysis used C (RFoff) as the RFoff representative
V_m retained only as 1000x10 subsample without unit metadata in B/C; none in A
H_trajectory is a population scalar, not per-neuron
